etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Borrowed from Latin praevāricātus, perfect active participle of praevāricor (“to walk crookedly; to play a false or double part”), from prae- + vāricō (“to stand with feet apart, straddle”), from vāricus (“with feet spread apart”); see -ate (verb-forming suffix).
senses: (transitive, intransitive, obsolete) To deviate, transgress; to go astray (from).
(intransitive) To speak or act in a manner that is intentionally ambiguous or evasive; equivocate.
